strings.ekumanov-forum-widgets.admin.settings.en: When enabled, each open and focused forum tab sends a small background ping. For logged-in users it keeps the "online" indicator fresh while they read or compose without navigating between pages (for example, during a long reply via the realtime extension); for guests (when guest counting is on) it's how the guest count is collected. Server load is negligible — both paths throttle their writes server-side, regardless of how many tabs are open. Disable if you do not want any background traffic.

strings.ekumanov-forum-widgets.admin.settings.la: How many minutes since last activity to consider a user online. Default: 5, which pairs with the presence heartbeat (enabled by default) — the heartbeat keeps activity fresh for users with a focused tab open, so active users won't drop off. If you disable the heartbeat, raise this to 10 or higher to avoid users blinking offline mid-session.
strings.ekumanov-forum-widgets.admin.settings.on: How long to cache the online users list. Two separate caches are maintained: one for privileged users (those with the "Always view user last seen time" permission, who can also see hidden users) and one for everyone else.

strings.ekumanov-forum-widgets.admin.settings.sh: When enabled, an approximate count of unauthenticated visitors is shown in the expanded panel as a dotted circle below the hidden users. Each guest tab pings a small endpoint that records a hash of the visitor's IP and User-Agent into a short-lived presence map; the count is the number of unique fingerprints seen within the "last seen interval". Counting is approximate — visitors behind a shared NAT collapse into one, mobile users on rotating IPs may be over-counted. No persistent identifier is stored on the visitor's browser.
Enable or disable the online users feature entirely. When disabled, no online user queries will be executed.

Automatically detect and flag spam content from new users. This system monitors posts and discussions from recently registered users for common spam indicators like phone numbers, email addresses, and suspicious URLs.

You have the option to report spammers to StopForumSpam in order to keep the greater forum community spam free.
When enabled, registrations from known Tor exit nodes will be automatically blocked. This can help prevent anonymous spam registrations, but may also prevent legitimate users who use Tor for privacy.

One per line, or comma separated. Registrations from these networks are refused outright, whether or not the address is listed. StopForumSpam returns the network number on every lookup, and almost nobody browses a forum from a hosting provider. Accepts 31272 or AS31272. Leave empty to record the network without acting on it.

The confidence score is a reasonably good indicator that the field under test would result in unwanted activity. Set your confidence level as a percentage. If the field is equal or above this figure, the registration will be blocked, regardless on the 'frequency' test above.
Pass a MD5 hash of the email address should you wish to not pass the email address itself. This method bypasses all blacklists, normalisation and obfuscation bypass checks.

The number of spam reports between all enabled checks that will trip the spam filter.
Ex: If the email has 1 hit, and the ip has 2 hits, there will be 3 hits in total. If the threshold is set to 3 or less we will prevent the registration.

Checks new user registrations against the StopForumSpam database. If either the confidence or frequency thresholds are reached, the user is prevented from completing their registration on your forum. SSO register via fof/oauth and fof/passport is also supported. Other SSO providers should work, but are untested.
StopForumSpam could not be reached (first failure {when}). Registrations are being allowed through unchecked until it recovers.
A sighting from years ago says little about whoever is registering today. 0 keeps every listing, however old. Blacklisted domains and networks are always honoured regardless of this.

By default we will direct the lookup to the closest regional server in order to provide the fastest response. Should you wish to restrict traffic to a specific region, such as for compliance with company or country privacy regulations, then you can force a connection to a specific region.

When StopForumSpam's own data blocks a registration, the attempt is reported back so the spammer's activity can be confirmed. Blocks from Tor or a denied network are never reported, as they are this forum's policy rather than evidence. Requires a StopForumSpam API key (see above).

If enabled, we will check the StopForumSpam database when a new user registers on your forum. If the user is found (username, IP address, email) and that data point is enabled along with the SFS confidence level reaching your defined level, they will be prevented from completing their registration.

strings.fof-pwa.admin.pwa.other.display_text:
How the app opens when launched from its icon:

Standalone: A separate app window without the browser's address bar.
Minimal UI: Like Standalone, with basic navigation such as back and reload.
Full screen: Uses the entire screen without browser controls.
Browser: Opens in a normal browser tab or window.

Browsers may use a fallback if the selected mode is not supported.
strings.fof-pwa.admin.pwa.other.heading: Other
strings.fof-pwa.admin.pwa.other.orientation_text:
Any: Let the app rotate with the device.
Natural: Use the device's usual orientation, typically portrait on phones and landscape on monitors.
Portrait: Keep the app vertical.
Landscape: Keep the app horizontal.

Portrait and Landscape each allow two positions, 180 degrees apart. Select a Primary or Secondary option to use just one. On a phone, Portrait (primary) usually means upright, and Portrait (secondary) means upside down. For landscape, which direction is primary depends on the device.

Some browsers and devices may ignore the selected orientation.

When used by a supported desktop browser, Window Controls Overlay takes precedence over the selected display mode.

If enabled, users can get a more immersive, native-like experience by hiding the native title bar. Whether Window Controls Overlay is actually applied depends on the user's preference and browser compatibility.
